Intelligence Sharing, No Off Switch

Twelve U.S. senators are trying to stop Congress from locking expanded defense and intelligence cooperation with Israel into law. One disputed provision would require more intelligence sharing and bar it from being “suspended, reduced, or otherwise materially limited.”

The eleven Democrats and independent Bernie Sanders argue that the fiscal 2027 bill would restrict Washington’s ability to protect sensitive information and reassess cooperation.

Two other provisions would create a joint defense technology initiative covering fields including AI, cyberwarfare, and autonomous systems. The senators warn that building Israeli technology into American weapons programs could give Israel leverage over future U.S. decisions. They cite Israel’s move to block the transfer of American Iron Dome batteries to Ukraine.

With Trump ending traditional military aid at the end of the year, Netanyahu calls the shift from aid to joint development a move toward “partnership.”
